purpose: Correction latency: when this publisher corrects a figure, how long until AI systems stop serving the old one? A metric nobody publishes, because it needs a dated corrections log and a repeatable probe. Both exist here.

observations.note: Cited corrections.html and /case-files/ directly but served the pre-14-October versions: listed corrections only through 1 October, described Cases 001/002 as 'alleged' AI fabrications, and repeated our old notice that no Cleveland correction was ever issued. On the substance it was right on its own: it reported the 26 July change (73.8 -> 73.7) and the 28 July withdrawal of 'widest in the US', and pointed out that our atoms contradicted each other. Latency so far: at least 2 days 21 hours after publication.

method: Each observation is one probe of one system on one date. Latency for a system = days from corrected_on to the first observation in which it serves the new value and no later observation serves the old one. Reported per system as a date and a day count, never averaged across systems.
